questions.question: A Multinational Corporation (MNC) is defined as a company that:
options: Operates exclusively within a single municipal district
Is owned and directed by the United Nations General Assembly
Produces goods exclusively for non-profit charitable donation
Owns or controls production of goods and services in more than one nation
questions.explanation: A Multinational Corporation (MNC) is a company that owns or controls production in more than one nation. MNCs set up offices and factories for production in regions where they can get cheap labour and other resources.

questions.subtopic: Why MNCs Set Up Production Globally
questions.question: Why do MNCs locate their production units in different countries across the globe?
options: To minimise the cost of production and maximise their profits by leveraging cheap labour, resources, and proximity to markets
To distribute 100% of their revenues as free aid to foreign citizens
Because their home countries have legally banned all factory manufacturing
To avoid communicating with international transport companies
questions.explanation: MNCs set up production where it is close to the markets; where there is skilled and unskilled labour available at low costs; and where the availability of other factors of production is assured. This is done so that the cost of production is low and the MNCs can earn greater profits.

questions.subtopic: Spreading of Production by an MNC
questions.question: In the NCERT example of an MNC manufacturing industrial equipment: the product is designed in the United States, parts are manufactured in China, and customer care is handled in India. Why is India preferred for customer care?
options: Because telephone calls are legally prohibited in other countries
Because India has no domestic industrial manufacturing factories
Because India has skilled, English-speaking youth and trained engineers available at competitive wage costs
Because customer care can only operate in tropical climates
questions.explanation: India has highly skilled engineers who can understand the technical aspects of production. It also has educated English speaking youth who can provide customer care services. And all this probably can mean 50-60 percent cost savings for the MNC.

questions.question: 'Foreign Investment' is defined as:
options: Gold coins purchased by ordinary domestic citizens in retail jewelry shops
Investment made by Multinational Corporations (MNCs) in physical assets like land, buildings, machines, and other equipment in another country
Loans provided by the central government to local village panchayats
Taxes paid by domestic retail shops to municipal corporations
questions.explanation: Money that is spent to buy assets such as land, building, machines and other equipment is called investment. Investment made by MNCs is called foreign investment. Any investment is made with the hope that these assets will earn profits.

questions.subtopic: Most Common Route for MNC Investment
questions.question: What is the most common route chosen by MNCs to establish and expand production in developing countries?
options: To construct brand new factories in deep uninhabited forests
To donate all manufacturing blueprints to municipal libraries
To buy up established local domestic companies and then expand their production network
To operate exclusively through postal money order catalog sales
questions.explanation: The most common route for MNC investments is to buy up local companies and then to expand production. MNCs with huge wealth can quite easily do so. For example, Cargill Foods, a very large American MNC, bought over Parakh Foods in India.

questions.subtopic: Example: Cargill Foods and Parakh Foods
questions.question: When American agribusiness giant Cargill Foods bought Parakh Foods in India, what valuable domestic asset did Cargill immediately acquire?
options: The entire sovereign fleet of the Indian Navy
Parakh Foods' extensive marketing network across India, well-known brand reputation, and five modern oil refineries
Exclusive mineral mining licenses in the Himalayas
The direct ownership of the Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation: Parakh Foods had built a large marketing network in various parts of India, where its brand was well-reputed. Also, Parakh Foods had four oil refineries, whose control now shifted to Cargill. Cargill became the largest producer of edible oil in India.

questions.question: In industries like garments, footwear, and sports goods, how do large MNCs typically control production across developing nations?
options: They place orders with thousands of small decentralized local producers worldwide and sell the finished products under their own powerful brand names
They hire foreign armies to operate sewing machines in village workshops
They manufacture 100% of all garments in automated factories in Europe
They purchase raw cotton and burn it to raise global clothing prices
questions.explanation: Large MNCs in developed countries place orders for production with small producers. Garments, footwear, sports items are examples of industries where production is carried out by a large number of small producers around the world. The MNCs sell these under their own brand names.

questions.subtopic: Impact of Foreign Trade on Domestic Markets
questions.question: What primary opportunity does foreign trade create for domestic producers in any country?
options: It prevents domestic producers from selling products within their home towns
It mandates that all goods must be gifted to foreign consumers for free
It forces manufacturers to convert factories into agricultural fields
It allows producers to reach beyond domestic borders and compete in international global markets
questions.explanation: Foreign trade creates an opportunity for the producers to reach beyond the domestic markets, i.e., markets of their own countries. Producers can sell their produce not only in markets located within the country but can also compete in markets located in other countries of the world.

questions.subtopic: Chinese Toys in India Case Study
questions.question: In the NCERT case study of Chinese toys imported into India, what was the primary impact on Indian toy manufacturers?
options: Indian toy makers instantly bought all toy factories in Beijing
Indian toy makers increased prices by 500% and quadrupled their sales
Indian toy makers faced severe competition, lost market share, and many had to shut down their workshops because Chinese toys were cheaper and offered newer designs
Chinese toys were completely rejected by Indian consumers
questions.explanation: Chinese toys became popular because of cheaper prices and new designs. Within a year, 70 to 80 percent of toy shops in India replaced Indian toys with Chinese toys. Indian toy makers suffered heavy business losses.

questions.question: 'Globalisation' is best defined as:
options: The complete closure of national borders to foreign travellers
The rapid process of international integration and interconnection between countries through trade, foreign investment, and technology flows
The division of the world into completely self-sufficient isolated communes
The mandatory adoption of a single world religion by all governments
questions.explanation: Globalisation is this process of rapid integration or interconnection between countries. MNCs are playing a major role in the globalisation process. More and more goods and services, investments and technology are moving between countries.

questions.question: How did the invention of intermodal freight containers revolutionize global trade transport?
options: Goods are packed into huge standardized containers that are transferred seamlessly across ships, railways, and trucks, slashing port handling costs and transit times
Containers can fly through the air using solar-powered magnetic levitation
Containers eliminate the need for container ships and railway tracks
Containers can only be opened by officials of the World Bank
questions.explanation: Containers for transport of goods: goods are placed in containers that can be loaded intact onto ships, railways, planes and trucks. Containers have led to huge reduction in port handling costs and increased the speed with which exports can reach markets.

questions.question: A tax imposed on imported goods by a national government is commonly referred to as a:
options: Subsidy grant
Foreign direct investment
Corporate dividend
Trade Barrier (Tariff)
questions.explanation: Tax on imports is an example of a trade barrier. It is called a barrier because some restriction has been set up. Governments can use trade barriers to increase or decrease (regulate) foreign trade and to decide what kinds of goods and how much of each should come into the country.

questions.question: Why did the Indian government put strict trade barriers on foreign imports following Independence in 1947?
options: Because the government wanted to bankrupt all domestic private businesses
Because international shipping ports did not exist in India before 1991
Because the United Nations ordered India to ban foreign commerce
To protect newly emerging domestic industries from foreign competition during their nascent infant stage
questions.explanation: The Indian government, after Independence, had put barriers to foreign trade and foreign investment. This was considered necessary to protect the producers within the country from foreign competition. Industries were just coming up in the 1950s and 1960s, and competition from imports at that stage would not have allowed these industries to survive.

questions.question: What major economic policy reform was adopted by the Government of India starting around 1991?
options: Liberalisation — removing barriers and restrictions on foreign trade and foreign investment to encourage global competition
Nationalisation of all privately owned consumer software companies
Complete prohibition of foreign multinational companies from entering India
Banning the export of Indian manufactured goods to overseas markets
questions.explanation: Starting around 1991, some far reaching changes in policy were made in India. The government decided that the time had come for Indian producers to compete with producers around the globe. Removing barriers or restrictions set by the government is what is known as liberalisation.

questions.question: What is the primary stated objective of the World Trade Organisation (WTO)?
options: To enforce a universal currency across all seven continents
To liberalise international trade and oversee that multilateral trade rules are obeyed by member nations
To command military peacekeeping troops in conflict zones
To provide direct cash unemployment doles to factory workers
questions.explanation: World Trade Organisation (WTO) is an organisation whose aim is to liberalise international trade. Started at the initiative of developed countries, WTO establishes rules regarding international trade, and sees that these rules are obeyed.

questions.question: What major unfair practice or debate surrounds the WTO regarding agricultural trade between developed and developing nations?
options: Developing nations have banned all American farm products from global trade
The WTO forces developed nations to pay 90% import duties on all industrial electronics
Developed nations like the USA force developing countries to remove agricultural tariffs while giving massive subsidies to their own rich farmers, artificially depressing global prices
American farmers are legally prohibited from exporting wheat to Asian markets
questions.explanation: In developed countries like the US, farmers receive massive government subsidies allowing them to dump farm goods abroad at artificially low prices, while developing nations were pressured to eliminate agricultural import barriers — a clear case of unfair trade.

questions.question: What special fiscal incentive is offered to companies setting up manufacturing units in Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in India?

Free imported luxury cars for all factory line workers
Direct representation in the state legislative assembly

questions.subtopic: Small Producers Hit by Global Competition
questions.question: In the NCERT case of Ravi, who manufactured electrical capacitors in Tamil Nadu, how did trade liberalisation affect his factory?
options: Ravi's company instantly acquired Samsung and Sony corporations
When the government removed import restrictions on capacitors, television makers imported cheaper components, causing Ravi's sales to drop by half and forcing him to fire workers
Ravi was appointed chief director of the World Trade Organisation
Ravi's factory output expanded by 1,000% within two months
questions.explanation: Ravi took a loan to start his unit manufacturing capacitors in 1992. When government removed trade barriers on imports of capacitors under WTO agreements, MNC television makers imported cheaper components. Ravi's production fell by half and he had to lay off half his workforce.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Economics, Chapter 4, Section 4.4 (Case of Ravi)

questions.question: 'Fair Globalisation' refers to a global economic order that:
options: Bans all international trade and eliminates shipping containers
Forces all multinational companies to give 100% of their shares to foreign governments
Requires developed nations to annex developing countries
Creates opportunities for all and ensures that the benefits of globalization are shared equitably among workers, small producers, and developing nations
questions.explanation: Fair globalisation would create opportunities for all, and also ensure that the benefits of globalisation are shared better. The government can play a major role in making this possible by supporting small producers and enforcing labour laws.
